title: The fibre functor is an equivalence
statement:
Let $Y$ be connected with a geometric point $\bar y\to Y$. Then the
fibre functor induces an equivalence

$$
F_{\bar y}:\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }
\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\text{-}\mathbf{Set},
$$

and likewise on $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ under the identification of
[thm-galois-lc-etale], where
$\pi_1(Y,\bar y)=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y})$ carries the profinite
topology of [def-galois-fibre-functor]; here $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ and the fibres are those of [def-galois-categories]. The equivalence is compatible
with finite limits and colimits. It is compatible with base change: for a morphism $f:Y'\to Y$ with $Y'$ connected and a geometric point $\bar y'$ of $Y'$ with $\bar y=f\circ\bar y'$, there is a continuous homomorphism $f_*:\pi_1(Y',\bar y')\to\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ such that $|(P\times_YY')_{\bar y'}|\cong|P_{\bar y}|$, naturally in $P\in\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$, as $\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$-sets, $\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$ acting on the right through $f_*$. If moreover $f$ is finite etale, then $f_*$ is injective and its image is the stabilizer of the point $\bar y'$ of $|Y'_{\bar y}|$, an open subgroup of $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ of finite index: base change to $Y'$ corresponds to the passage to this open subgroup.

proof.text: *The equivalence on $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$.* By [lem-fet-galois-category] the pair $(\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y),F_{\bar y})$, $F_{\bar y}(P)=|P_{\bar y}|$, is a Galois category. By [thm-galois-abstract-equivalence], with $G=\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y}|_{\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)})$, the functor $P\mapsto|P_{\bar y}|$ with its $G$-action is an equivalence of $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ with the finite sets with continuous $G$-action, $G$ being profinite by [lem-galois-aut-profinite]. The group $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ of [def-galois-fibre-functor] is the automorphism group of the fibre functor on $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$; the equivalence $\Phi:\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\to\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ of [thm-galois-lc-etale] comes with an isomorphism $F_{\bar y}\circ\Phi\cong F_{\bar y}$, and conjugation by $\Phi$ and this isomorphism is an isomorphism $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\cong G$ of groups compatible with the evaluation embeddings into $\prod\operatorname{Aut}(F_{\bar y}(-))$ (the factors indexed by $P$ and by $\Phi(P)$ are identified, and every object of $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ is isomorphic to some $\Phi(P)$), hence a homeomorphism. So $F_{\bar y}:\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\to\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$ is an equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 0BND (pione-theorem-fundamental-group) (1), proof: 'Part (1) follows from Lemma 0BNB and Proposition 0BN4'

proof.text: *The equivalence on $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$.* By [thm-galois-lc-etale] the functor $\Phi:P\mapsto\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_Y(-,P)$ is an equivalence $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)\to\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ compatible with the fibre functors, $\Phi(P)_{\bar y}\cong|P_{\bar y}|$ naturally in $P$; by [def-galois-fibre-functor] $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ acts on $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ by evaluation, and the isomorphism $\Phi(P)_{\bar y}\cong|P_{\bar y}|$ is $\pi_1$-equivariant by the definition of the identification in step 1. Hence $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ on $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$ is isomorphic to the composite of a quasi-inverse of $\Phi$ with the equivalence of step 1, and is an equivalence $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)\to\pi_1(Y,\bar y)\text{-}\mathbf{Set}$.

source.place: Remark 0DV6 (etale-cohomology-remark-functorial-locally-constant-on-connected): the equivalence for finite locally constant sheaves of sets follows from the diagram of Theorem 0BND

proof.text: *Finite limits and colimits.* $\mathrm{F\acute Et}(Y)$ has finite limits and finite colimits (axiom 1 of a Galois category, [lem-fet-galois-category]), and so has $\mathrm{FLC}(Y)$, being equivalent to it. The equivalences of steps 1 and 2 preserve all limits and colimits that exist, by [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits]; in particular a finite limit or colimit of finite etale covers (fibre products, finite coproducts, quotients by finite groups) is sent to the corresponding limit or colimit of finite continuous $\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$-sets.

source.place: SGA 1 V §7, p. 115: 'Cette equivalence permet donc d'interpreter les operations courantes de limites projectives et limites inductives finies sur des revetements ... en termes des operations analogues dans C(pi)'

proof.text: *Base change.* Let $f:Y'\to Y$ with $Y'$ connected, $\bar y'$ a geometric point of $Y'$ and $\bar y=f\circ\bar y'$. By [lem-galois-pi1-functoriality] there is a continuous homomorphism $f_*:\pi_1(Y',\bar y')\to\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ and bijections $\tau_P:|(P\times_YY')_{\bar y'}|\to|P_{\bar y}|$, natural in $P$, with $f_*(g)\tau_P(z)=\tau_P(gz)$; this is the asserted isomorphism of $\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$-sets. (By the same lemma the equivalence of step 1 for $Y'$, composed with base change, is the equivalence of step 1 for $Y$ followed by restriction of the action along $f_*$.)

source.place: Theorem 0BND (pione-theorem-fundamental-group) (3) and its proof via Lemma 0BN5 (pione-lemma-functoriality-galois)

proof.text: *Finite etale base change: the open subgroup.* Let moreover $f$ be finite etale. Then $f_*$ is injective by [lem-galois-pi1-finite-etale-injective], and its image is the stabilizer $U$ of $\bar y'\in|Y'_{\bar y}|$, an open subgroup of index $\#|Y'_{\bar y}|$, finite by [def-galois-categories], by [lem-galois-pi1-finite-etale-image-stabilizer]. Hence $f_*$ is a continuous bijection of the compact group $\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$ onto the Hausdorff group $U$, so a homeomorphism (both are profinite by [lem-galois-aut-profinite], for the topologies of [def-galois-fibre-functor]), and by step 4 base change to $Y'$ followed by $F_{\bar y'}$ is $F_{\bar y}$ followed by restriction of the action to $U\cong\pi_1(Y',\bar y')$.

source.place: SGA 1 V §7, p. 116, last paragraph ('Si en particulier S' est un revetement etale de S, alors l'homomorphisme u est un isomorphisme de pi_1(S',a') sur le sous-groupe ouvert ... stabilisateur U de a' in F_a(S')'), and Proposition V.6.13
